title: workload-sculptor-and-autotune-harness-for-prefill-decode-scheduling
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Spike + engineering work to build a flexible benchmarking harness (Workload Sculptor) that can: 1) synthesize and replay realistic mixed workloads by sculpting token lengths, prompt distributions, and API mix; 2) autotune kernel selection and prefill/decode cadence per model/hardware profile; 3) produce artifactized golden baselines and deterministic deltas for CI perf gates. Goal is to reduce manual tuning when onboarding new model variants and to prevent regressions in tail latency and p99 token-cost during CI changes.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can generate 5 canonical workload templates (chat-short, chat-long, completion-burst, embedding-bimodal, streaming-mix) and export deterministic seeds
End-to-end autotune run completes for at least 3 model families (Llama-2 13B, Mistral-like 7B, Bloom-like 3B) on two hardware types (A100, H100) and emits kernel-choice profiles
Produced golden baseline artifacts (metrics JSON + sample traces) and a diff tool that flags >5% p99 regression or >10% cost-per-token change
CI job integrated that runs a lightweight sculptor mix on every runtime change and posts pass/fail status with links to artifacts
Documentation and quickstart (README + example GH action) merged and a demo run recorded on the perf dashboard

notes: Motivation: current golden baselines are brittle and require manual selection of kernel routes when models or quantization profiles change. We need an automated way to propose kernel mappings and scheduling hints per workload.
Scope decision (2026-02-05): limit initial autotune to kernel selection and prefill pacing; full quantization knob sweep postponed to follow-up epic.
Determinism approach: use seed-locking + request-canonicalization (strip non-deterministic headers) so golden diffs focus on runtime behavior not request noise.
Trade-offs considered: heavy autotune runs give better mappings but are costly; we will gate full autotune to nightly runs and use a fast heuristic pass for PR CI.
Success metric: reduce time-to-stable-kernel-mapping for new model onboarding from weeks to <= 3 days and reduce incidence of CI false positives by 60%.
Implementation note: prefer existing bench infra (mixbench) for replay engine compatibility, but keep sculptor outputs as standalone JSON seeds for portability.

postmortem_learnings: From initial runs: kernel choices that reduce median often trade-off against memory fragmentation under certain prefill patterns. We must include memory pressure as a first-class autotune signal.
Deterministic seeding reduced noise in diffs but we need to canonicalize timing metadata to avoid irrelevant timestamp churn in artifacts.
